classification.difficultyReason: Part b requires identifying the trapezoidal cross-section, subtracting its parallel sides to obtain a right-triangle leg, applying Pythagoras, then combining end areas and lateral faces.

content.prompt: Calculate the surface area of the following shapes.

spec.description: Right triangular prism with length 20 cm and perpendicular triangular-end sides 6 cm and 8 cm. Retains the right-angle marker and dashed hidden edges. Ordinary source blue and red strokes are rendered black, with hidden edges distinguished by dashes.
spec.mathematics: The triangular end has perpendicular sides 6 cm and 8 cm. Its third side is not supplied. The prism length is 20 cm.

answer.worked:
The third side of the triangular end is $s$.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}\\s&=10\text{ cm}\\A_{\text{ends}}&=2\times\frac12\times6\times8\\A_{\text{ends}}&=48\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{rectangles}}&=20(6+8+10)\\A_{\text{rectangles}}&=480\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=48+480\\A_{\text{total}}&=528\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Trapezoidal prism with horizontal parallel cross-section sides 8 cm and 20 cm, vertical left side 5 cm, sloping right side and prism length 15 cm. Retains visible face boundaries and dashed hidden edges. Ordinary source colours are replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: The right trapezium has height 5 cm and parallel sides 8 cm and 20 cm. The prism length is 15 cm. The sloping cross-section side is not supplied.

answer.worked:
The horizontal difference between the parallel sides is $20-8=12\text{ cm}$. Let the sloping side be $s$.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}\\s&=13\text{ cm}\\A_{\text{ends}}&=2\times\frac{8+20}{2}\times5\\A_{\text{ends}}&=140\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{rectangles}}&=15(8+20+5+13)\\A_{\text{rectangles}}&=690\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=140+690\\A_{\text{total}}&=830\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
